question: I remember us-east-1 buckets could have names up to 255 characters with uppercase letters. Can I still create one like that today?

gold.answer: No. Since March 1, 2018, new buckets in US East (N. Virginia) must follow the same rules as every other Region: 3 to 63 characters, lowercase letters, numbers, periods and hyphens only. Names of up to 255 characters with uppercase letters and underscores were only possible before that date.

Bucket names must be between 3 (min) and 63 (max) characters long.

question: Can I build a new integration against the Amazon S3 SOAP API?

gold.answer: No. The S3 SOAP APIs are not available to new customers and reach end of life on August 31, 2025. SOAP over HTTP is deprecated (existing use is HTTPS only) and new S3 features are not supported for SOAP. Use the REST API or the AWS SDKs.

question: Our function runs on a runtime that Lambda deprecated last month. Will Lambda stop invoking it?

gold.answer: No. You can continue to invoke functions on a deprecated runtime indefinitely. But AWS may no longer apply security patches or updates to that runtime, the functions are no longer eligible for technical support, and AWS strongly recommends migrating to a supported runtime.
support: After a runtime is deprecated, AWS may no longer apply security patches or updates to that runtime, and functions using that runtime are no longer eligible for technical support. While you can continue to invoke your functions indefinitely, AWS strongly recommends migrating to a supported runtime.

notes: A common wrong belief is that deprecated runtimes stop being invokable.

question: I just opened a new AWS account. Do I get the standard 1,000 concurrent executions for Lambda right away?

gold.answer: Not necessarily. New AWS accounts have reduced concurrency and memory quotas for Lambda functions, and AWS raises them automatically based on usage. The documented default of 1,000 concurrent executions, which can be increased to tens of thousands, is the quota for established accounts.
support: New AWS accounts have reduced concurrency and memory quotas for Lambda Functions and Lambda MicroVMs. AWS raises these quotas automatically based on your usage.

Since December 31, 2024 all new domains are created with the updated Amazon SageMaker Studio as the default.

gold.answer: Elasticsearch 7.10 reaches end of standard support on November 7, 2027. After that it is on extended support, with the updated end date of November 7, 2030, and you are charged a flat extended support fee per Normalized Instance Hour on top of the standard instance cost.

question: Our legacy client only speaks TLS 1.0. Can it call the EC2 API in a Region that launched in 2024?

gold.answer: No. AWS Regions launched after October 30, 2021 do not support Amazon EC2 API requests over connections established with TLSv1, TLSv1.1, or unencrypted HTTP.
support: AWS Regions launched after October 30, 2021 will no longer support Amazon EC2 API requests over connections that are established using TLSv1, TLSv1.1, or unencrypted HTTP.

question: Is the Fargate on-demand burst launch rate the same 100 tasks in every Region?

gold.answer: No. For Regions introduced after May 20, 2025 the Fargate On-Demand burst launch rate maximum is 25; the other supported Regions have 100. The quota is adjustable.
support: The maximum number of on-demand Amazon ECS tasks or Amazon EKS pods launched in a single burst (burst rate) in this account in the current region. Note: For Regions introduced after May 20, 2025, the maximum is 25

question: Can I launch a new RDS DB instance on magnetic (standard) storage to save money?

gold.answer: No. Magnetic storage is deprecated and no longer offered for new DB instances, and starting July 1, 2026 you can no longer restore a snapshot to magnetic storage. Use General Purpose SSD or Provisioned IOPS SSD.
support: Magnetic storage is deprecated and is no longer offered for new DB instances. Starting July 1, 2026, you can no longer restore a snapshot to magnetic storage. Use General Purpose SSD or Provisioned IOPS SSD for any new storage needs.

question: I created my AWS account in September 2025. Do I get 750 free hours per month of db.t3.micro on RDS for 12 months?

gold.answer: No. The 12-month RDS Free Tier (750 hours each month of Single-AZ db.t3.micro and db.t4g.micro running MySQL, MariaDB or PostgreSQL) continues only for accounts that were AWS Free Tier customers before July 17, 2025. Free Tier resources created after July 17, 2025 use the new AWS Free Tier offering.

question: Does AWS AppSync only offer GraphQL APIs?

gold.answer: No. As of March 13, 2025 you can also build a real-time publish/subscribe API over WebSockets with AWS AppSync Events, alongside the GraphQL APIs.

question: Is DynamoDB point-in-time recovery fixed at 35 days?

gold.answer: No. You can set the recovery period for continuous backups to any number between 1 and 35 days (RecoveryPeriodInDays). Changing the window does not change the price: PITR is charged on table size regardless of the recovery period.

Changing the recovery window (for example, from 35 days to 1 day) doesn't reduce the price. The cost remains the same regardless of the recovery period you choose.

question: Is the public IPv4 address that EC2 assigns to my running instance free?

gold.answer: No. AWS charges for all public IPv4 addresses, including public IPv4 addresses associated with running instances and Elastic IP addresses. Elastic IP addresses are charged whether they are in use or idle.

question: When I create an Amazon Bedrock Knowledge Base, do I have to choose an embedding model and run my own vector store?

A Customer-managed Knowledge Base is the variant where you set up and manage your own RAG pipeline, including the vector store.

question: Is 15 minutes still the absolute maximum run time for a Lambda invocation?

gold.answer: Not in every case. The standard function timeout maximum is 900 seconds (15 minutes). Functions using AWS Lambda Managed Instances support a maximum of 5,400 seconds (90 minutes) for asynchronous invocations and event source mapping invocations, except Amazon MQ and Amazon DocumentDB.
